permit.applies: The performer applies for the visa, at a Nigerian embassy or through the e-Visa portal, on the event organiser's invitation.
permit.first: An invitation letter from the event organiser.

sources.title: Consulate General of Nigeria, Johannesburg, Visas: Artist(e)/Entertainer/Musician Visa – F7F
sources.said: ARTIST(E)/ENTERTAINER/MUSICIAN VISA – F7F Artist(e) Entertainer/ Musician Visa is a single-entry visa issued to visit Nigeria for the purpose of performance as an artist(e), entertainer or musician Visa Category Short Visit Visa Sub category Exchange, Journalism, Religious, Sports & Entertainment Eligibility Performing artist(e)s entertainers or musicians Requirements Passport valid for at least 6 months with at least 2 blank visa pages for endorsement Invitation letter from event organizer Return ticket Evidence of sufficient funds Evidence of hotel reservation/host address in Nigeria Visa Validity Valid for not more than 90 days from the date of issuance Permit Type and duration of Stay Single entry. Visitors Permit not exceeding 90 days Permited Activicties Permitted to create/perform play, art, entertainment, music, dance, drama, comedy and other activities in the creative industry Restricted Activicties Not permitted for work Permitted Visa Channels Embassy e-Visa

note: Route read again on a Nigerian mission's own page: the Consulate General in Johannesburg lists it as 'Artist(e)/Entertainer/Musician Visa – F7F' (NIS calls the same class 'Creative Arts Visa – F7F'), a single-entry short visit visa that lets a performer perform; the same page marks it 'Not permitted for work', i.e. it covers the performance only, not other employment.
